The Independent National Electoral Commission has said that it will not take any action on the Federal High Court judgment nullifying the leadership of the African Democratic Congress until it obtains a certified true copy of the ruling. INEC National Commissioner and Charman of Information and Voter Education Committee, Mohammed Haruna, disclosed this on Wednesday during a webinar organised by the PUNCH Media Foundation, explaining that the Commission needed to study the judgment and obtain legal advice before deciding its next move. The judgment, delivered on November 5 by Justice Peter Lifu of the Federal High Court in Abuja, nullified the emergence of the Senator David Mark-led ADC leadership and invalidated decisions taken under it, including the process that produced former Vice-President Atiku Abubakar as the party’s presidential candidate for the 2027 election. The ruling followed a suit filed by a former Deputy National Chairman of the party, Nafiu Bala Gombe, who challenged the emergence of the Mark-led leadership. The ADC has rejected the judgment and appealed the decision. It also filed an application for a stay of execution and urged INEC not to take any consequential action while the appeal is pending. He explained that the Commission had already taken steps to obtain the document but could not compel the court to issue it immediately. “We can’t rush the courts, but we do our own part. We have a whole legal department. As soon as judgments like this come, what they do, of course, is to go to the courts, to go to the court register, to see if they can obtain it. But they have their own processes,” he said. 2027: Tackle fake news early, Yiaga urges INEC 2027: Yiaga Africa urges INEC to tackle AI misinformation 2027: Police vow crackdown on AI-generated disinformation According to him, it usually takes about a week to obtain a certified true copy of a judgment. Haruna noted that the judgment was delivered towards the end of the previous week, adding that the Commission would begin its internal review once the document was received. “So, as soon as we get it, we run a committee system. The department which is in charge of litigation will look into it, then they will advise. There is a committee which is chaired by a national commissioner. They, in turn, will advise the Commission itself, and then the Commission will take a decision on exactly what to do,” he said. He added that the Commission could not take a decision on the matter until it received the certified true copy. “So, for now, until we receive that certified true copy, there’s really nothing that we can do about it,” he said.
